items.quote: The microstructures of the alloys after quenching (ascast from arc-melting) and after the DTA measurements were examined by electron microscopy.

items.applies_to: four alloys with the compositions Ca33Mg33Si33, Ca34Mg16Si50, Ca25Mg21Si54 and Ca34Mg50Si16 (at.%)
items.quote: Thermal analysis was performed on four alloys with the compositions Ca33Mg33Si33, Ca34Mg16Si50, Ca25Mg21Si54 and Ca34Mg50Si16 (at.%) using a Netzsch DTA 404 apparatus. The pre-molten sample was sealed under argon by welding in a tantalum crucible to avoid evaporation and oxidation. The DTA measurements were carried out under vacuum with heating/cooling rates of 5 K/min and 1 K/min. Each sample was heated and cooled several times for the precise determination of peak positions. The estimated error of measurements is 5 K.
The measurements were performed using a Siemens D5000 diffractometer with a step 0.02  of 2   and 3 s exposition time in the point.

items.label: Eighteen samples
items.quote: Eighteen samples with different compositions were prepared. All alloy compositions are given in Table 3. The alloys were carefully arc melted under purified argon to avoid extensive evaporation of Mg and Ca. Starting materials were Ca granules (99.5 mass% Alfa, Karlsruhe), Mg pieces (99.98 mass% Alfa, Karlsruhe) Si chips (99.9998 mass%, Wacker, Burghausen).
